Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 4 days of upper respiratory symptoms (initial sore throat and runny nose progressing to nasal congestion and new dry cough), intermittent headaches, myalgias, fatigue, night sweats, and initial fever now improving; assessed as likely viral URTI/early influenza; supportive care and safety-net follow-up advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 4 days of feeling unwell.
- Timeline:
  - Day 1–2: Sore throat with painful swallowing; improved/resolving.
  - Early course: Runny nose; now predominantly nasal congestion.
  - Day 3–4: New dry, constant cough (onset yesterday).
  - Throughout: Fatigue/tiredness; night sweats for 3–4 days; intermittent generalized headaches.
  - Fever present initially; improved with paracetamol/ibuprofen.
- Exposures: Close contact with a sneezing colleague (possible exposure from her children in kindergarten).
- Respiratory: Mild exertional shortness of breath; no dyspnea at rest; no chest pain.
- ENT: No ear pain or discharge. Did not examine throat; no observed exudates reported.
- Neuro/vision: No visual changes; no photophobia.
- GI/GU: No nausea/vomiting; bowels and urine normal.
- Appetite/fluids: Slightly reduced appetite; increased fluid intake.
- Skin/MSK: No rash; myalgias/aches started in past couple of days.
- Self-care: Using paracetamol and ibuprofen with symptom relief.
- Work/activities: Continues working; slower productivity; avoiding gym due to exertional breathlessness.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported; otherwise fit and well.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Medications: Paracetamol and ibuprofen for fever/symptoms — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Occupation: Accountant; working during illness; increased workload/stress around year-end, described as manageable.
- Tobacco: Occasional cigars at company parties; not a regular smoker.
- Alcohol: Occasional/social use; not a heavy drinker (patient initially said “No,” then “occasionally yes”—conflict noted).
- Exercise: Typically attends gym; currently avoiding due to exertional breathlessness.

Family History:
- Grandmother with diabetes mellitus, likely type 2 (patient believes type 2).
- Great-grandfather with eczema.

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- None performed or reviewed during this consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Viral upper respiratory tract infection / possible early influenza
  - Assessment: 4-day history with sore throat (improving), rhinorrhea progressing to congestion, new dry cough, myalgias, fatigue, night sweats, and initial fever responding to OTC analgesics/antipyretics; exposure to sick contact; no red flag features on review.
  - Plan:
    - Rest; consider 1–2 days off work.
    - Increase oral fluids.
    - Continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Expect gradual improvement over ~7–10 days.
    - Safety-net: Seek care sooner for high/persistent fever, worsening/labored breathing, or chest pain.
    - Follow-up: Return next week if not improving.

- Issue 2: Dry cough (onset yesterday)
  - Assessment: Likely viral; no chest pain; no rest dyspnea.
  - Plan:
    - Conservative symptomatic management as above.
    - Avoid strenuous exercise until symptoms improve.

- Issue 3: Night sweats and intermittent headaches
  - Assessment: Associated with acute viral illness; present 3–4 days; no visual symptoms or photophobia.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor; managed as part of viral illness plan above.

- General plan items:
  - Patient understands advice and agrees to rest, hydrate, and monitor symptoms with planned follow-up and safety-net instructions.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals; no physical examination findings; no comprehensive medication list beyond OTCs; vaccination status (influenza/COVID) not documented; smoking quantity and alcohol units not quantified.
- Internal conflicts: Alcohol use—patient initially denied, then reported occasional/social use (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/overlaps; clinically adequate information captured.
